_comment: Theseus transport, then linear probing: the transported delta is applied to the target backbone at alpha, the backbone is frozen, and only the zero-shot classification head is refit on a few-shot support set. The probe starts from the zero-shot head, so its epoch-0 log line is the plain zero-shot accuracy of the *transported* backbone -- everything above that is what probing adds.
_support_set: theseus/bico have no few-shot knob of their own (they use num_batches), so linear_probe_shots_per_class is set explicitly here -- without it the run stops with an error rather than guessing a support-set size.
_head_at_eval: The probed head replaces the zero-shot head for BOTH the target_zeroshot and rebased columns, so those columns keep isolating what the transport did -- the classifier is identical on both sides.
_lr_note: linear_probe_lr must stay small relative to the head's own scale: rows are L2-normalized (entries ~1/sqrt(D)), and Adam's step is ~lr per coordinate regardless of gradient magnitude, so a large lr erases the zero-shot head in a couple of steps and the probe restarts from nothing.
